messages.subject: plyr::join fails when joining-by large number of variables
parts:
I noticed some strange behavior using 'join' in plyr.
I am having the same problem both under R 2.13.1 under windows (tested
on both plyr 1.5.2 and plyr 1.6) and R 2.13.2 under cygwin (plyr 1.6).
Here is some reproducible code that triggers the same error:
#=============================
library(plyr)
df1 <- data.frame(a1=c(1,2), a2=c(1,2), a3=c(1,2), a4=c(1,2),
a5=c(1,2), a6=c(1,2), a7=c(1,2), a8=c(1,2), a9=c(1,2), a10=c(1,2),
a11=c(1,2), a12=c(1,2), a13=c(1,2), a14=c(1,2), a15=c(1,2),
a16=c(1,2), a17=c(1,2), a18=c(1,2), a19=c(1,2), a20=c(1,2),
a21=c(1,2), a22=c(1,2), a23=c(1,2), a24=c(1,2), a25=c(1,2),
a26=c(1,2), a27=c(1,2), a28=c(1,2), a29=c(1,2), a30=c(1,2),
a31=c(1,2), a32=c(1,2), a33=c(1,2), a34=c(1,2), a35=c(1,2),
a36=c(1,2), a37=c(1,2), a38=c(1,2), a39=c(1,2), a40=c(1,2),
a41=c(1,2), a42=c(1,2), a43=c(1,2), a44=c(1,2), a45=c(1,2),
a46=c(1,2), a47=c(1,2), a48=c(1,2), a49=c(1,2), a50=c(1,2), x=c(1,2))

df2 <- data.frame(a1=c(1,2), a2=c(1,2), a3=c(1,2), a4=c(1,2),
a5=c(1,2), a6=c(1,2), a7=c(1,2), a8=c(1,2), a9=c(1,2), a10=c(1,2),
a11=c(1,2), a12=c(1,2), a13=c(1,2), a14=c(1,2), a15=c(1,2),
a16=c(1,2), a17=c(1,2), a18=c(1,2), a19=c(1,2), a20=c(1,2),
a21=c(1,2), a22=c(1,2), a23=c(1,2), a24=c(1,2), a25=c(1,2),
a26=c(1,2), a27=c(1,2), a28=c(1,2), a29=c(1,2), a30=c(1,2),
a31=c(1,2), a32=c(1,2), a33=c(1,2), a34=c(1,2), a35=c(1,2),
a36=c(1,2), a37=c(1,2), a38=c(1,2), a39=c(1,2), a40=c(1,2),
a41=c(1,2), a42=c(1,2), a43=c(1,2), a44=c(1,2), a45=c(1,2),
a46=c(1,2), a47=c(1,2), a48=c(1,2), a49=c(1,2), a50=c(1,2), y=c(3,4))

df1
df2

merge(df1, df2) # works fine
join(df1, df2, type="inner") # returns error
#=============================

The error I am getting is:
Joining by: a1, a2, a3, a4, a5, a6, a7, a8, a9, a10, a11, a12, a13,
a14, a15, a16, a17, a18, a19, a20, a21, a22, a23, a24, a25, a26, a27,
a28, a29, a30, a31, a32, a33, a34, a35, a36, a37, a38, a39, a40, a41,
a42, a43, a44, a45, a46, a47, a48, a49, a50
Error in .Call("split_indices", index, group, as.integer(n)) :
negative length vectors are not allowed
In addition: Warning messages:
1: In structure(as.integer(res), n = attr(res, "n")) :
NAs introduced by coercion
2: In split_indices(seq_along(keys$y), keys$y, keys$n) :
NAs introduced by coercion

I would be grateful is somebody could run the code above and confirm
that the error is not limited to my machine.

By the way: the error message changes depending on the number of
variables. For example running the join on 30 variables (a1...a30)
instead of 50 variables (a1..a50) results in the following error
('merge' still works fine):

Joining by: a1, a2, a3, a4, a5, a6, a7, a8, a9, a10, a11, a12, a13,
a14, a15, a16, a17, a18, a19, a20, a21, a22, a23, a24, a25, a26, a27,
a28, a29, a30
Error in .Call("split_indices", index, group, as.integer(n)) :
cannot allocate vector of length 1073741824

Thanks,
Dario

Joining by: a1, a2, a3, a4, a5, a6, a7, a8, a9, a10, a11, a12, a13,

parts:
Thank you Hadley.
I just downloaded the development version, and the reproducible code
works fine now.

Unfortunately the join on the real data still does not work as expected.
The program no longer fails due to memory issues, but the results are
not correct.
The 'merge(a, b)' command run on the real data returns a dataframe
with 8601 rows.
The 'join(a, b, type="inner")' command run on the same data returns a
dataframe with 80293 rows instead.

I will try to create a short reproducible example to duplicate the
problem, but so far I had no luck.

Are 'merge(a, b)' and 'join(a, b, type="inner")' supposed to return
the same result in plyr 1.6?
Thanks,
Dario

messages.subject: Re: plyr::join fails when joining-by large number of variables
parts:
Here is a reproducible example of the error I mentioned in my last post.
Unfortunately the behavior of plyr::join is quite unpredictable on my
machine, and I was able to reproduce the error only using semi-real
data (comma delimited text file, see below).
Please note that the code does not work in plyr 1.6, probably due to
the bug that has just been fixed by Hadley (see email chain).
The code works in plyr 1.6_develop, but the result is incorrect on my machine.

Instructions:
1. download foo.csv at https://gist.github.com/1282106
2. run the following code using the development version of plyr 1.6:
#=======
library(plyr)

foo <- read.csv("foo.csv") # 1000 unique records
nrow(join(foo, foo, type="inner")) # returns 1240 rows (incorrect result)
nrow(merge(foo, foo)) # returns 1000 rows (correct result)
#=======

So far I tested the code under cygwin using r 2.13.2.
I would be grateful is somebody else could run the code above and
confirm that the error is reproducible.

One thing I noticed is that the order of the columns affects the result:
#=======
library(plyr)

foo <- read.csv("foo.csv") # 1000 unique records
foo <- foo[ ,c(2:11,1)] # moving the first column to the end of the data.frame
nrow(join(foo, foo, type="inner")) # returns 1000 rows (correct result)
nrow(merge(foo, foo)) # returns 1000 rows (correct result)
#=======

Dario
